influence_policy: No citation added by this pass establishes authorial influence. Relationship notes control interpretation.

W3C-PROV.citation: W3C. *PROV-O: The PROV Ontology*. W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013.
W3C-PROV.note: Adjacent provenance standard; it models entities, activities, and agents, but does not by itself establish the paper's stronger authority or standing claims.

IN-TOTO.citation: Santiago Torres-Arias et al. "in-toto: Providing Farm-to-Table Guarantees for Bits and Bytes." *28th USENIX Security Symposium*, 2019, pp. 1393-1410.
IN-TOTO.note: Predecessor supply-chain lineage system used for comparison; no influence claim is made unless the source head already documents one.

SLSA.citation: OpenSSF. *Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts (SLSA), Version 1.2*. 2026.
SLSA.note: Adjacent software-supply-chain assurance standard, especially relevant to provenance and verification boundaries.

PCC.citation: George C. Necula. "Proof-Carrying Code." *POPL '97*, 1997, pp. 106-119. DOI: 10.1145/263699.263712.
PCC.note: Predecessor for binding machine-checkable evidence to executable artifacts; the present paper may demand broader semantic or constitutional obligations.

COMPCERT.citation: Xavier Leroy. "Formal Verification of a Realistic Compiler." *Communications of the ACM* 52(7), 2009, pp. 107-115. DOI: 10.1145/1538788.1538814.
COMPCERT.note: Predecessor verified-compilation result used to distinguish proven translation preservation from broader governance claims.

ABSTRACT-INTERPRETATION.citation: Patrick Cousot and Radhia Cousot. "Abstract Interpretation: A Unified Lattice Model for Static Analysis of Programs by Construction or Approximation of Fixpoints." *POPL '77*, 1977. DOI: 10.1145/512950.512973.
ABSTRACT-INTERPRETATION.note: Predecessor formal framework for sound approximation and fixpoint reasoning.

TLA.citation: Leslie Lamport. *Specifying Systems: The TLA+ Language and Tools for Hardware and Software Engineers*. Addison-Wesley, 2002.
TLA.note: Predecessor specification discipline for state machines, safety, liveness, and refinement.

SALTZER-SCHROEDER.citation: Jerome H. Saltzer and Michael D. Schroeder. "The Protection of Information in Computer Systems." *Proceedings of the IEEE* 63(9), 1975, pp. 1278-1308. DOI: 10.1109/PROC.1975.9939.
SALTZER-SCHROEDER.note: Foundational protection principles used as a comparison point for least authority, mediation, and inspectability.

OCAP.citation: Mark S. Miller. *Robust Composition: Towards a Unified Approach to Access Control and Concurrency Control*. PhD dissertation, Johns Hopkins University, 2006.
OCAP.note: Predecessor object-capability treatment of authority and compositional security.

SEL4.citation: Gerwin Klein et al. "seL4: Formal Verification of an OS Kernel." *SOSP '09*, 2009, pp. 207-220. DOI: 10.1145/1629575.1629596.
SEL4.note: Predecessor for machine-checked implementation correspondence and capability-based kernel design.

CHERI.citation: Robert N. M. Watson, Simon W. Moore, Peter Sewell, and Peter G. Neumann. *An Introduction to CHERI*. University of Cambridge Technical Report UCAM-CL-TR-941, 2019. DOI: 10.48456/tr-941.
CHERI.note: Adjacent capability architecture demonstrating unforgeable hardware authority and compartmentalization.

REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.citation: Reproducible Builds Project. *Formal Definition of Reproducible Builds*.
REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.note: Adjacent reproducibility practice; byte reproduction is compared with, but not equated to, semantic or constitutional continuity.

LOCAL-FIRST.citation: Martin Kleppmann et al. "Local-First Software: You Own Your Data, in Spite of the Cloud." *Onward! 2019*, pp. 154-178. DOI: 10.1145/3359591.3359737.
LOCAL-FIRST.note: Adjacent local-first design program relevant to user custody, offline operation, and collaboration.

GNU-FREEDOM.citation: Free Software Foundation. *The Free Software Definition*.
GNU-FREEDOM.note: Normative predecessor for user freedoms; the paper may add reconstruction, governance, or hardware-boundary obligations beyond license rights.

OSI-OSD.citation: Open Source Initiative. *The Open Source Definition*.
OSI-OSD.note: Adjacent licensing baseline; source availability is not treated as sufficient for operational sovereignty.

RAG.citation: Patrick Lewis et al. "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks." *NeurIPS 2020*. arXiv:2005.11401.
RAG.note: Predecessor retrieval architecture; comparison centers on provenance, admission, and fail-closed constraints not supplied by retrieval alone.

REACT.citation: Shunyu Yao et al. "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models." *ICLR 2023*. arXiv:2210.03629.
REACT.note: Predecessor agent pattern for interleaving reasoning and action; used to distinguish action traces from governed effects.

CONSTITUTIONAL-AI.citation: Yuntao Bai et al. "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback." 2022. arXiv:2212.08073.
CONSTITUTIONAL-AI.note: Adjacent use of constitutional language in model alignment; comparison prevents conflating training-time behavioral rules with executable institutional governance.

NIST-AI-RMF.citation: Elham Tabassi. *Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)*. NIST AI 100-1, 2023. DOI: 10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1.
NIST-AI-RMF.note: Adjacent risk-management framework used to test whether the paper operationalizes governance beyond voluntary process guidance.

OECD-AI.citation: OECD. *Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence*. OECD/LEGAL/0449, adopted 2019 and updated 2024.
OECD-AI.note: Adjacent policy standard for accountability, traceability, transparency, safety, and human-centered values.

STOCHASTIC-PARROTS.citation: Emily M. Bender et al. "On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big?" *FAccT '21*, 2021. DOI: 10.1145/3442188.3445922.
STOCHASTIC-PARROTS.note: Counterpressure concerning scale, environmental cost, documentation, and social risk; included to prevent governance proposals from becoming capability-only narratives.

RDF.citation: Richard Cyganiak, David Wood, and Markus Lanthaler, eds. *RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax*. W3C Recommendation, 25 February 2014.
RDF.note: Adjacent graph data model and identity baseline.

SKOS.citation: Alistair Miles and Sean Bechhofer, eds. *SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference*. W3C Recommendation, 18 August 2009.
SKOS.note: Adjacent standard for concepts, labels, schemes, notes, and semantic mappings.

OWL.citation: W3C OWL Working Group. *OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Document Overview*, Second Edition. W3C Recommendation, 11 December 2012.
OWL.note: Adjacent formal ontology standard used to compare declared semantics and inference commitments.

FAIR.citation: Mark D. Wilkinson et al. "The FAIR Guiding Principles for Scientific Data Management and Stewardship." *Scientific Data* 3, 2016, 160018. DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2016.18.
FAIR.note: Predecessor stewardship principles for findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reuse.

CONCEPTUAL-SPACES.citation: Peter Gardenfors. *Conceptual Spaces: The Geometry of Thought*. MIT Press, 2000.
CONCEPTUAL-SPACES.note: Predecessor geometric treatment of concepts; cited as comparison, not as validation of the paper's manifold terminology.

OSTROM.citation: Elinor Ostrom. *Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action*. Cambridge University Press, 1990. DOI: 10.1017/CBO9780511807763.
OSTROM.note: Predecessor institutional account of rule-governed collective action and polycentric governance.

CONSTITUTIONALISM.citation: Wil Waluchow and Dimitrios Kyritsis. "Constitutionalism." *Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy*, substantive revision 2023.
CONSTITUTIONALISM.note: Adjacent legal-philosophical account of limited authority; included to expose differences between political and computational constitutionalism.

LESSIG-CODE.note: Predecessor argument that software architecture regulates behavior; the paper's contribution may be to make such regulation inspectable and revisable.

RFC8785.citation: Anders Rundgren, Bret Jordan, and Samuel Erdtman. *JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)*. RFC 8785, 2020.
RFC8785.note: Adjacent canonicalization standard relevant to stable cryptographic commitments.

RFC9162.citation: Ben Laurie et al. *Certificate Transparency Version 2.0*. RFC 9162, 2021.
RFC9162.note: Adjacent append-only Merkle-log standard for inclusion and consistency evidence.

DID-CORE.citation: Manu Sporny et al., eds. *Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0*. W3C Recommendation, 19 July 2022.
DID-CORE.note: Adjacent decentralized identity standard; identifier resolution is not assumed to settle semantic standing or jurisdiction.

LAMPORT-CLOCKS.citation: Leslie Lamport. "Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System." *Communications of the ACM* 21(7), 1978, pp. 558-565. DOI: 10.1145/359545.359563.
LAMPORT-CLOCKS.note: Foundational predecessor for partial order, causality, and distributed event ordering.

BYZANTINE.citation: Leslie Lamport, Robert Shostak, and Marshall Pease. "The Byzantine Generals Problem." *ACM Transactions on Programming Languages and Systems* 4(3), 1982, pp. 382-401. DOI: 10.1145/357172.357176.
BYZANTINE.note: Predecessor fault model for agreement under adversarial or inconsistent participants.

CRDT.citation: Marc Shapiro et al. *A Comprehensive Study of Convergent and Commutative Replicated Data Types*. INRIA Research Report RR-7506, 2011.
CRDT.note: Predecessor convergence model for replicated state; convergence is compared with, but not equated to, legitimacy or semantic agreement.

NIST-CPS.citation: Edward R. Griffor et al. *Framework for Cyber-Physical Systems: Volume 1, Overview*. NIST SP 1500-201, 2017. DOI: 10.6028/NIST.SP.1500-201.
NIST-CPS.note: Adjacent cyber-physical systems framework for trustworthiness, timing, data, and lifecycle concerns.

NASA-RTA.citation: J. Tanner Slagel et al. "A Formal Verification Framework for Runtime Assurance." *NASA Formal Methods*, 2024. NASA NTRS 20230017350.
NASA-RTA.note: Adjacent runtime-assurance formalization, useful for comparing failover safety with constitutional admission and effect recognition.

STPA.citation: Nancy G. Leveson and John P. Thomas. *STPA Handbook*. MIT, 2018.
STPA.note: Adjacent systems-theoretic hazard analysis method; used to test treatment of unsafe control and system-level constraints.

MLETR.citation: UNCITRAL. *Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records*. United Nations, 2017.
MLETR.note: Adjacent legal standard for control, integrity, functional equivalence, and cross-border electronic records.

VVSG.citation: U.S. Election Assistance Commission. *Voluntary Voting System Guidelines, Version 2.0*. 2021.
VVSG.note: Adjacent voting-system standard for auditability, software independence, evidence, accessibility, and dispute resolution.

ISO8601.citation: International Organization for Standardization. *ISO 8601-1:2019, Date and time - Representations for information interchange - Part 1: Basic rules*. 2019.
ISO8601.note: Adjacent civil-time representation standard; comparison separates notation from governance of calendars and epochs.

TREASURY-TAX.citation: U.S. Department of the Treasury. *Tax Expenditures*. Office of Tax Analysis.
TREASURY-TAX.note: Primary official baseline for the definition and estimation limits of U.S. federal tax expenditures.

MARKOWITZ.citation: Harry Markowitz. "Portfolio Selection." *The Journal of Finance* 7(1), 1952, pp. 77-91. DOI: 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x.
MARKOWITZ.note: Predecessor risk-return optimization model; included to distinguish scalar optimization from governance-aware admissibility.

KALMAN.citation: Rudolf E. Kalman. "A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems." *Journal of Basic Engineering* 82(1), 1960, pp. 35-45. DOI: 10.1115/1.3662552.

POMDP.citation: Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra. "Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains." *Artificial Intelligence* 101(1-2), 1998, pp. 99-134. DOI: 10.1016/S0004-3702(98)00023-X.
POMDP.note: Predecessor model for acting under partial observability; used to compare belief-state control with governed epistemic state.

CHALMERS.citation: David J. Chalmers. "Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness." *Journal of Consciousness Studies* 2(3), 1995, pp. 200-219.
CHALMERS.note: Foundational framing of the explanatory gap; cited to bound, not resolve, phenomenal claims.

IIT4.citation: Larissa Albantakis et al. "Integrated Information Theory (IIT) 4.0: Formulating the Properties of Phenomenal Existence in Physical Terms." *PLOS Computational Biology* 19(10), 2023, e1011465. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011465.
IIT4.note: Competing formal theory of consciousness included for explicit contrast and counterevidence obligations.

GNW.citation: Stanislas Dehaene and Jean-Pierre Changeux. "Experimental and Theoretical Approaches to Conscious Processing." *Neuron* 70(2), 2011, pp. 200-227. DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2011.03.018.
GNW.note: Competing global-workspace account included to prevent a corpus-native ontology from substituting for empirical neuroscience.

RSA.citation: Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Marieke Mur, and Peter A. Bandettini. "Representational Similarity Analysis - Connecting the Branches of Systems Neuroscience." *Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience* 2, 2008, 4. DOI: 10.3389/neuro.06.004.2008.
RSA.note: Predecessor empirical method for comparing representational geometries.

LOCATELLO.citation: Francesco Locatello et al. "Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations." *PMLR* 97, 2019, pp. 4114-4124.
LOCATELLO.note: Counterevidence showing that desired latent factorization is not identifiable from unsupervised data without inductive biases.

USACE-SOIL.citation: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. *Sediment Investigations*, Engineer Manual EM 1110-2-4000. 14 February 2025.
USACE-SOIL.note: Primary engineering guidance for material characterization and classification; included to ground classification claims in field and laboratory practice.

EPA-SOIL.citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. *Guidance for Cleaning Up Groundwater, Soil and Air at Hazardous Waste Cleanup Facilities*.
EPA-SOIL.note: Primary remediation guidance emphasizing media transfer, exposure, and site-specific cleanup decisions.

SCA-CVA.citation: Specialty Coffee Association. *Coffee Value Assessment and Published Standards*.
SCA-CVA.note: Industry standard for repeatable physical, descriptive, affective, and extrinsic coffee assessment.

RFC8493.citation: John Kunze et al. *The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)*. RFC 8493, 2018.
RFC8493.note: Adjacent custody and transfer format for payload manifests, fixity, and complete package movement.

OAIS.citation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems. *Reference Model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS)*. CCSDS 650.0-M-3, Issue 3, December 2024.
OAIS.note: Predecessor preservation model for information packages, representation information, and designated communities.

IPFS.citation: Juan Benet. "IPFS - Content Addressed, Versioned, P2P File System." 2014. arXiv:1407.3561.
IPFS.note: Predecessor content-addressed network architecture; content identity is compared with, not treated as sufficient for, semantic jurisdiction.

BPE.citation: Rico Sennrich, Barry Haddow, and Alexandra Birch. "Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units." *ACL 2016*, pp. 1715-1725. DOI: 10.18653/v1/P16-1162.
BPE.note: Predecessor subword tokenization method used as a contrast to semantically governed token boundaries.

SENTENCEPIECE.citation: Taku Kudo and John Richardson. "SentencePiece: A Simple and Language Independent Subword Tokenizer and Detokenizer for Neural Text Processing." *EMNLP 2018: System Demonstrations*. DOI: 10.18653/v1/D18-2012.
SENTENCEPIECE.note: Predecessor tokenizer implementation used to separate statistical segmentation from semantic admissibility.

MDL.citation: Peter D. Grunwald. *The Minimum Description Length Principle*. MIT Press, 2007.
MDL.note: Predecessor theory of compression and model selection; compression is not assumed to preserve governance or meaning.

PARNAS.citation: David L. Parnas. "On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules." *Communications of the ACM* 15(12), 1972, pp. 1053-1058. DOI: 10.1145/361598.361623.
PARNAS.note: Foundational modularity treatment used to compare information hiding with explicit semantic and governance interfaces.

TECH-DEBT.citation: Ward Cunningham. "The WyCash Portfolio Management System." *OOPSLA '92 Experience Report*, 1992. DOI: 10.1145/157709.157715.
TECH-DEBT.note: Original technical-debt metaphor used to distinguish implementation debt from semantic debt.

OPENTELEMETRY.note: Adjacent observability standard for traces, metrics, logs, and context propagation; telemetry is not equated with adjudicated evidence.

TRACE-CONTEXT.citation: W3C. *Trace Context, Level 1*. W3C Recommendation, 23 November 2021.
TRACE-CONTEXT.note: Adjacent distributed tracing standard for propagating trace identity across service boundaries.

NIST-SSDF.citation: Karen Scarfone, Murugiah Souppaya, and Donna Dodson. *Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1*. NIST SP 800-218, 2022. DOI: 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218.
NIST-SSDF.note: Adjacent secure-development framework for preparation, protection, production, and vulnerability response.

FLYWHEEL.citation: Thomas Bowen, Ilya Chernyakhovskiy, Kaifeng Xu, Sika Gadzanku, and Kamyria Coney. *USAID Grid-Scale Energy Storage Technologies Primer*. NREL/TP-6A20-76097, 2021. DOI: 10.2172/1808490.
FLYWHEEL.note: External engineering baseline for flywheel architecture, response, lifetime, and energy-versus-power tradeoffs.

DIRECT-TORQUE.citation: Thomas G. Habetler et al. "Direct Torque Control of Induction Machines Using Space Vector Modulation." *IEEE Transactions on Industry Applications* 28(5), 1992, pp. 1045-1053. DOI: 10.1109/28.158828.
DIRECT-TORQUE.note: Predecessor electromechanical torque-control method; included to force clear differentiation from any novel reactor claim.
